problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only".
